newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT - JGBs seen underpinned by investor demand.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - JGBs seen underpinned by investor demand.

text.p: Japanese government bond (JGB) futures are expected to maintain a firm tone in Tokyo on Thursday, supported by strong investor demand for cash JGBs.
"The benchmark June futures contract is likely to test 126.00 today. However, profit-taking pressures are expected to intensify above that level," said a brokerage house trader.
Traders said any downside is likely to be limited due to investors' interest in buying cash JGBs.
"The demand-supply balance is tight. So bargain-hunting is likely to emerge on dips," said a trader at a city bank's securities unit.

"Over four trillion yen worth of JGBs are expected to mature in June. Also, the Housing Loan Administrative Corp will make a loan repayment of 1.2 trillion yen to agricultural financial bodies at the end of March. These are supportive factors for JGBs," said the second trader.

Agricultural financial bodies are expected to eventually invest this money into bonds, traders said. Traders said Japan's gross domestic product (GDP) data for the October-December period is unlikely to have a strong impact on the market.
The data will be released at 3.30 p.m. (0630 GMT).
Economists polled by Reuters said on average they expect real GDP to grow 0.8 percent quarter-on-quarter. The GDP grew 0.1 percent quarter-on-quarter in the previous quarter.
GDP forecasts ranged from 0.3 percent to 1.2 percent growth.
"People are not paying that much attention to old data. They are more interested in economic indicators for April or after to see the impact of the consumption tax hike," said the trader.
Japans' consumption tax will be raised to five percent from three percent on April 1.
